title: [CRY2-1] Commit streams are keyed to `channelToken`, so the sequencer rule forks the group across a
description: Review finding CRY2-1: Commit streams are keyed to `channelToken`, so the sequencer rule forks the group across an admission-key rotation (lens CRY2). Location: spec/05-messaging.md:27, 256; spec/14-jmap.md:157-162, 207, 238; spec/10-relays.md:839. Fix: The cited text holds as described. The sequencer admits any registered, not yet deregistered `keyEpoch` (14-jmap.md:207: "`channelToken` and `keyEpoch` MUST match a key registered under its agreement and not deregistered"). Registrations carry nothing that links tokens (10-relays.md:807), so the sequencer cannot restrict Commits to the newest stream. The committer reads only "that stream's log" (05-messaging.md:27). One partial mitigation already exists: 14-jmap.md:162 says "The total order of a channel's sequenced operations is by stream, in the order of the channel's tokens, then by position". That gives members a defined cross-stream comparison if "lower `n`" in 05:27 is read as that order. It does not save the committer-side check, and the 5-second switch window does not cover a k-stream Commit stamped up to 300 s after a (k+1)-stream Commit was applied. The "Closing a stream" rule (14-jmap.md:238) depends on the `after` field of `JmapSet`, which Commits do not carry, so it does not extend to Commits by itself. Under (a), 05:27 and 14-jmap §14.4.2 change to name the commit stream by a CO-issued `commitStreamID` in `ChannelAdmissionKey`, kept across rotations. Linking key epochs Full text: notes/review2/CRY2-verified.md and notes/review2/CRY2.md.
